value:
Read fallback for a reference that does not resolve (#202, v1.4.0). interpolateForRead in src/utils/interpolate.ts is the one helper: every `get` path, reverie_get and interpolateObject go through it. A read returns the stored text and warns; `run` still throws.

GOTCHAS — each one shipped in the PR and was caught in review, 2026-11-25:
- It falls back ONLY on UnresolvedReferenceError (missing, not-a-value, encrypted, too-deep) and StoreUnreadableError. A catch-all reported every other error as a chain nested too deeply. StrictInterpolationError (`:?`, a cycle) and any fault propagate.
- The scan must GO ON past an unresolved reference: the `tolerated` collector is threaded through interpolate and resolveRef. Returning at the first one let a value with a missing reference followed by a `:?` guard exit 0.
- `seen.size === 0` means the value being read, or one of its `:-` defaults. A failure further down gets `via` (the reference written in this entry that leads there), and no advice to escape it here.
- lint's seed-quality landmine heuristic asks interpolateForRead (it throws = landmine), so it cannot also list what a read returns as written.
- lint takes listUnreadableFiles() BEFORE any pass that resolves references: a lookup is project-first and registers the project store's unreadable files, which made `lint -G` fail on a project file.
- The set-time check lives in the command (src/index.ts), not in setEntry, and is handed only a value that may be shown. The warning quotes the reference; #230 ran it on a masked `--prompt` value too and printed part of a secret (fixed by #233). The masked value stays in a variable of its own (shownValue is undefined) — a flag would leave the data flow, and CodeQL, in place. Encrypted values are skipped.
- A batch `set a=… b=…` is checked once after the last pair, inside the last pair's instrumented call — in JSON mode that is the batch's one envelope.
- TEST TRAP: the dollar-brace pass finishes before the dollar-paren pass starts, so a value mixing an unresolved dollar-brace reference with an exec reference never reached the exec phase. A "never executes" test built on it passed with execution switched on. Use an exec-only value and mutation-check it (allowExec=true in interpolateForRead must fail three tests).
- MCP determineHit substring-matches MISS_PATTERNS over the whole response — the value and a user-written reference name included. Only a warning's fixed clauses are ours to keep clean.
See [[arch.interpolation]] for the exec invariant, [[context.unreadableStoreFiles]].
